title: Compatibility tuner and runtime fingerprint workflow for expert-model kernels
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Goal: Implement a lightweight compatibility tuner and runtime fingerprinting workflow that automates selection and publishing of best-fit compiled kernels for asymmetric expert architectures (MoE/GQA/MHA variants). Scope includes: a compile fingerprint format, an automated micro-benchmark harness that runs on onboarding hosts, a decision engine that proposes a pinned kernel revision per model+arch+quant config, and a publish pipeline that creates a signed profile in the model catalog. Out of scope for this ticket: full UI in Console (follow-up), and dedicated autoscaler integrations.
acceptance_criteria: Define a deterministic compile fingerprint scheme (arch, CUDA, driver, compute capability, quant profile, batch/seq distribution) documented in Confluence.
Automated harness runs on onboarding infra and uploads per-kernel latency/throughput/alloc telemetry to the onboarding bucket.
Decision engine outputs a recommended kernel revision and a compatibility score for MoE/GQA/MHA variants.
Publish pipeline creates a signed performance profile JSON and uploads to the model catalog service with artifact link and runtime-1.22 tag.
Safety: when a published profile fails runtime health checks, automatic rollback to the previous signed profile within 5 minutes must be possible.
End-to-end test demonstrating a canary rollout at 5% with telemetry gating (p99 latency, error rate, and token cost) must exist in CI.
implementation_notes: Fingerprint format: <arch>-<cuda>-<driver>-<cc>-<quant>-<seqdist>-<batchdist>-<kernel_hash>. We'll generate kernel_hash from deterministic build inputs (compiler flags + kernel source tree hash + ISA features).
Micro-benchmark harness: reuse existing harness in infra/benchmarks with added MoE routing trace generator and synthetic GQA sparsity patterns; output standardized CSV and JSON artifacts.
Decision heuristics: primary objective p99 latency under target SLO; secondary objectives: token cost and memory headroom. Weighted score: 0.6*p99_norm + 0.25*cost_norm + 0.15*mem_norm.
Fallback policy: if model receives >10% regression on p99 or >0.5% increase in error_rate in canary window, trigger instant rollback and label profile as 'unstable' in catalog.
Compatibility checks: ensure quant profile compatibility (int8/4bit paths), fallback to higher-precision kernel when quant mismatch detected. Add a compatibility matrix entry for each kernel profile.
Store signed profile: use existing signing lambda (infra/sec-sign) and include metadata: created_by, job_id, benchmark_commit, grafana_snapshot_url.
Integrations: shipping hooks to catalog API (POST /profiles), runtime will read profile by model_id + pinned_profile_tag at request start.
Data retention: keep per-benchmark telemetry for 90 days for regressions analysis; longer retention archived on request.
testing_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint generator and deterministic kernel_hash computation.
Integration test that runs the micro-benchmark on a small GPU instance in CI and validates artifact schema matches catalog contract.
E2E canary test: simulate production traffic with recorded MoE routing traces and assert telemetry gates (p99 <= baseline*1.08, error_rate delta <= 0.2%).
Chaos scenario: simulate driver upgrade (CUDA +/- minor) and verify compatibility table prevents publishing incompatible profiles.
Load soak: run 6-hour throughput soak for selected kernel profile to detect rare OOMs or memory leaks.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): local harness and fingerprint verifier. Manual publish to staging catalog.
Phase 1 (canary): 5% traffic for 24h. Gate on p99, error_rate, token_cost. Auto-rollback enabled.
Phase 2 (ramp): 25% traffic for 48h if canary is healthy. Monitor for tail latency regressions and KV cache hit-rate reduction.
Phase 3 (global): 100% traffic after two successful ramps and two-week monitoring window. Mark profile as stable and create follow-up ticket for Console exposure.
Emergency rollback: documented script (tools/profile-rollback) that runtime on-call can execute to revert to previous signed profile across regions.
notes_and_tradeoffs: We favor deterministic fingerprints over heuristic tags to avoid ambiguous matches; cost is added complexity in build pipelines.
Decision engine is heuristic-based for MVP to iterate quickly; long-term plan is ML-ranking from fleet telemetry (future ticket).
We accept some duplication of profiles (same kernel for multiple seqdist bins) to reduce risk of brittle routing heuristics.
Quant path complexity: supporting every quant variant increases compile matrix exponentially — initial release will support int8 and fp16; 4-bit on selective models after telemetry thresholds.
